title: Application viewport size accelerator commands

equivalent_mutants.reason: Checked against hash-verified v1.0 (see application_viewport_accelerators.notes.md): the mutant tests +0x30 in place of +0x2c, so the first test repeats the second. Outcomes differ only when +0x2c is zero and +0x30 is not; the mutant then calls 0x42a630, which reads the same zero +0x2c and returns 0 at 0x42a63a without stores or calls, so the function returns 0 with no memory effect, as the original does. Only scratch ECX differs, and the sole callers (0x427541 and 0x427564) overwrite EAX and never read ECX. A Unicorn probe of the byte-patched original matched memory and preserved registers in all 36 runs per function.

Checked against hash-verified v1.0 (see application_viewport_accelerators.notes.md): the caller passes (size,1,1) to 0x429ed0, which reads +0x68 only at 0x429ef1 to pick between two branches that both reach 0x429f02 because its second argument is 1 (0x429ef6-0x429efc), then stores its clamped size to +0x68 at 0x429f05 before any call. Dropping the caller's own store therefore leaves the whole machine state identical from 0x429f08 on; a Unicorn probe of the original with the store replaced by NOPs matched all memory and registers at 0x429f08 for 21 sizes per function.
